title: Humanity in the Image of God
summary: What it means to be human: made in God's image, male and female, body and soul, for God's glory.
description: Who are we? This course studies the biblical doctrine of humanity: our creation in God's image, the dignity and equality of every person, male and female as God's design, the unity of body and soul, our calling to work and rule as God's stewards, and how Christ, the true image of God, restores what sin has marred.
objectives: Explain what it means that humans are made in God's image
Show the dignity and equal worth of every person
Present biblical teaching on male and female, body and soul
Show how Christ restores the image of God in believers
outcomes: Explain the image of God from Genesis 1:26-28
Apply human dignity to issues such as ethnicity, disability and the unborn
Describe the main views on body, soul and spirit
Explain the creation mandate to work and rule
Describe how believers are renewed in Christ's image

modules.title: Made in God's Image
modules.intro: Humans are the high point of creation, made in the image and likeness of God. This week we ask what that means.

lessons.title: Let us make man
lessons.body:
On the sixth day God said, "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion" (Genesis 1:26). God formed Adam from the dust and breathed into him "the breath of life; and man became a living soul" (Genesis 2:7).

Humans are part of creation, made from the earth, yet different from all other creatures. Only humans are made in God's image, given personal fellowship with God, and given responsibility to rule creation.

We are not accidents or merely advanced animals. We are made by God, for God.

lessons.title: What is the image of God?
lessons.body:
Scripture does not define the image in one sentence, but it includes several connected ideas:

- **Likeness:** humans reflect God's character in reason, morality, creativity, relationships and love (Colossians 3:10; Ephesians 4:24).
- **Relationship:** we were made to know God and to live in fellowship with Him and others.
- **Representation:** like a king's statue in a province, humans represent God's rule on earth (Genesis 1:26-28).

The image was damaged by the fall but not destroyed; after the flood, murder is still forbidden "for in the image of God made he man" (Genesis 9:6; James 3:9).

lessons.title: The dignity of every person
lessons.body:
Because every person bears God's image, every person has dignity and worth. This includes the poor (Proverbs 14:31), people of every ethnicity, for God "hath made of one blood all nations of men" (Acts 17:26), the disabled, the elderly and the unborn, knit together in the womb by God (Psalm 139:13-16).

It rules out tribalism, racism, contempt for the weak, and abuse. Cursing people made in God's likeness is condemned (James 3:9-10).

The image of God is the foundation of human rights and of Christian compassion.

terms.def: The way humans reflect and represent God, setting them apart from other creatures.
Latin for 'image of God'.
Adam's state after God breathed life into him: a living person.
The worth every person has because they bear God's image.
Paul's phrase showing all nations share one human origin.
The sacred value of human life from conception to natural death.

texts.teaches: God created man in His own image, male and female.
God breathed into man the breath of life and he became a living soul.
Murder is forbidden because man is made in God's image.
God made of one blood all nations of men.
God knit us together in our mother's womb.

summary: Humans are made in God's image, unlike all other creatures.
The image includes likeness, relationship and representation.
The image was damaged by sin but not destroyed.
Every person, of every tribe and condition, has God-given dignity.

questions.q: What does Genesis 9:6 give as the reason murder is wrong?
options: Man is made in God's image
All nations are of one blood
Only Israel is made by God

questions.q: Was the image of God destroyed by the fall?
Which idea compares humans to a king's statue in a province?

modules.title: Male and Female
modules.intro: God created humanity male and female. This week we study the equality and the differences God designed.

lessons.title: Equal in worth
lessons.body:
"So God created man in his own image... male and female created he them" (Genesis 1:27). Both man and woman bear God's image fully. Both received the blessing and the commission to rule (1:28).

In Christ, "there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus" (Galatians 3:28); husbands and wives are "heirs together of the grace of life" (1 Peter 3:7).

Any teaching or custom that treats women as less human, or as property, contradicts Scripture.

lessons.title: Different by design
lessons.body:
Genesis 2 shows God making the man first, then the woman as "an help meet for him", one who corresponds to him (2:18). *Help* is not a lowly word; it is used of God Himself helping Israel (Psalm 33:20).

Man and woman are made for each other and complete each other, physically, emotionally and in calling. God brought the woman to the man, and marriage was born: the two "shall be one flesh" (Genesis 2:24).

Our sex is a gift of God, part of His good design, not something to be despised or rejected.

lessons.title: Roles in home and church
lessons.body:
Bible-believing Christians agree on equal worth; they differ on how roles work out.

- **Complementarian view:** men and women are equal in worth but have different roles; husbands lead in loving, sacrificial headship and wives respect and submit (Ephesians 5:22-33), and the office of pastor/elder is for qualified men (1 Timothy 2:12; 3:2). Most Baptist churches and Deeper Life hold this.
- **Egalitarian view:** headship texts are read in their cultural setting, and all roles in home and church are open to both men and women according to gifting (Acts 2:17-18; Romans 16:1-7).

Both views reject domination and abuse, and call for mutual love and service (Ephesians 5:21).

terms.def: A helper suitable for, corresponding to, the man (Genesis 2:18).
The deep union of husband and wife in marriage.
The view that men and women are equal in worth with distinct God-given roles.
The view that all roles in home and church are open to both sexes by gifting.
The husband's responsibility to lead with Christlike, sacrificial love.
Believers' humble service to one another in the fear of God (Ephesians 5:21).

texts.teaches: God made a helper suitable for the man.
A man shall cleave to his wife and they shall be one flesh.
In Christ there is neither male nor female; all are one.
Husbands and wives are heirs together of the grace of life.
Husbands are to love their wives as Christ loved the church.

summary: Man and woman are equally made in God's image.
They are different by design and made to complement each other.
Complementarians and egalitarians differ on roles but agree on equal worth.
All Christians reject domination and call for mutual love.

questions.q: Who is called a "help" in Psalm 33:20, showing the word is not lowly?

options: All are one in Christ Jesus

questions.q: Which view holds equal worth with distinct roles?
What do both complementarians and egalitarians reject?

modules.title: Body, Soul and Spirit
modules.intro: What are we made of? This week we look at the material and immaterial parts of human nature.

lessons.title: Two views: two parts or three?
lessons.body:
Scripture speaks of humans as body and soul, or body, soul and spirit. Christians hold two main views:

- **Dichotomy:** we have two parts, body and soul (or spirit), with "soul" and "spirit" often used for the same inner self (Matthew 10:28; Ecclesiastes 12:7). Common among Baptists and Reformed writers.
- **Trichotomy:** we have three parts: body, soul (mind, emotions, will) and spirit (the part that relates to God), drawn from 1 Thessalonians 5:23 and Hebrews 4:12. Common in many Pentecostal and Holiness churches, including Deeper Life.

Both agree we have a real physical body and a real inner self that survives death.

lessons.title: The body is good
lessons.body:
Our bodies are not prisons for the soul, as some Greek philosophers taught. God made the body, called it good, and will raise it. "Know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost?... glorify God in your body" (1 Corinthians 6:19-20).

This gives value to health, work, rest, food and the care of the sick. It also calls for sexual purity and self-control (1 Thessalonians 4:3-5).

At death body and soul separate for a time; at the resurrection believers receive glorified bodies (1 Corinthians 15:42-44; Philippians 3:21).

lessons.title: The heart
lessons.body:
The Bible often speaks of the **heart** as the centre of the person: where we think, feel, choose and worship. "Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life" (Proverbs 4:23).

Sin corrupts the heart (Jeremiah 17:9), and Jesus taught that evil comes from within (Mark 7:21-23). God promises a new heart (Ezekiel 36:26).

True religion is not only outward. God "looketh on the heart" (1 Samuel 16:7) and asks for our love "with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind" (Matthew 22:37).

terms.def: The view that a human being has two parts: body and soul (spirit).
The view that a human being has three parts: body, soul and spirit.
The inner, immaterial self; in trichotomy, the mind, emotions and will.
The inner self; in trichotomy, the part that relates to God.
In Scripture, the centre of the person: thought, feeling, will and worship.
The believer's body, indwelt by God's Spirit.

texts.teaches: May your whole spirit, soul and body be preserved blameless.
Men can kill the body but not the soul.
The believer's body is the temple of the Holy Ghost.
Keep your heart, for out of it are the issues of life.
The heart is deceitful above all things.

summary: Christians hold dichotomy (body and soul) or trichotomy (body, soul and spirit).
Both views affirm a real body and a real inner self that survives death.
The body is good, a temple of the Holy Ghost, and will be raised.
The heart is the centre of the person and needs God's renewal.

questions.q: Which verse is the main basis for trichotomy?
What does 1 Corinthians 6:19 call the believer's body?
options: The temple of the Holy Ghost

questions.q: In Scripture, the heart is mainly:
options: Only the organ that pumps blood

questions.q: What happens to believers' bodies at the resurrection?

modules.title: Our Calling and Restoration
modules.intro: God gave humanity a calling to work and rule. Sin marred the image, but Christ restores it. This week we see both.

lessons.title: The creation mandate
lessons.body:
God blessed Adam and Eve: "Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion" (Genesis 1:28). He put Adam in the garden "to dress it and to keep it" (2:15).

Work was given before the fall; it is part of our dignity, not a curse. Farming, building, teaching, trading, art and science can all honour God. "Whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord" (Colossians 3:23).

Dominion is not domination. We rule as stewards under God, caring for creation and for people.

lessons.title: Christ, the true image
lessons.body:
Christ is "the image of the invisible God" (Colossians 1:15), "the express image of his person" (Hebrews 1:3). In Him we see what God is like and what humanity was meant to be.

As the last Adam (1 Corinthians 15:45), He obeyed where Adam failed, and He fulfils Psalm 8's vision of man crowned with glory (Hebrews 2:6-9).

To know what true humanity looks like, look at Jesus: perfectly loving God and neighbour, holy, humble, faithful.

lessons.title: Renewed in His image
lessons.body:
Salvation restores the image of God in us. Believers are "predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son" (Romans 8:29). We "have put on the new man, which is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him" (Colossians 3:10).

This renewal is gradual now: "we all... are changed into the same image from glory to glory" (2 Corinthians 3:18).

It will be complete when Christ appears: "we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is" (1 John 3:2). Our destiny is not to become gods but to be fully human, as God intended, in Christ.

terms.def: God's command to be fruitful, fill the earth and rule it as stewards.
Humanity's responsible rule over creation under God.
One's calling to serve God through work and life.
Christ, who succeeded where the first Adam failed.
Being shaped into the likeness of Christ.
The renewed self of the believer, created after God's image.

texts.teaches: God commanded humanity to be fruitful, fill and rule the earth.
Do all your work heartily, as to the Lord.
Christ is the image of the invisible God.
Believers are predestined to be conformed to Christ's image.
When Christ appears, we shall be like Him.

summary: God gave humanity a calling to fill the earth, work and rule as stewards.
Work is part of human dignity, not a curse.
Christ is the true image of God and the last Adam.
Believers are being renewed in His image and will be like Him when He appears.

questions.q: Was work given before or after the fall?
Who is called "the image of the invisible God"?
To whose image are believers being conformed?
What does dominion mean in Genesis 1?

short.q: What does it mean that humans are made in the image of God?
short.model: Humans reflect God's character, are made for relationship with Him, and represent His rule on earth, unlike any other creature.

short.q: How should the image of God shape how we treat people of other tribes?
short.model: Every person has equal dignity because all bear God's image and are of one blood, so tribalism and contempt are sin; we must respect and love all.

short.q: Explain the difference between dichotomy and trichotomy.
short.model: Dichotomy teaches two parts (body and soul); trichotomy teaches three (body, soul and spirit).

short.q: Why is the human body important in Christian teaching?
short.model: God created it good, it is the temple of the Holy Ghost, and it will be raised; so we glorify God in our bodies.
God's command to be fruitful, fill the earth and rule it as stewards, working and caring for creation.

short.q: How does Christ restore the image of God?
short.model: Believers are being renewed and conformed to Christ's image now, and will be like Him when He appears.

lists.q: List three aspects of the image of God taught in this course.
List four groups whose dignity the image of God protects.
List the three parts of a person in trichotomy.

assignments.title: Dignity in practice
assignments.prompt: Choose one group often treated without dignity in your society (for example house helps, people with disabilities, widows, the unborn, or people from another tribe). Using the doctrine of the image of God, explain what Scripture teaches about their worth and what a Christian response should look like.

assignments.title: Work as worship
assignments.prompt: Describe your work, study or daily responsibilities. Using Genesis 1-2 and Colossians 3:23-24, explain how they can be done as service to God, and one change you will make.
